findings.summary: no diffuse arm cleared the other arms' marks, and has_diffuse_render_texture WINS at binding resolution in both PALs (pal_sdl_gpu.cpp returns the render-target view before consulting base_color_texture, and turns a stale mark into a hard gpu_error in the main pass; pal_dawn.cpp reads it the same way) -- so `diffuseTexture = rtt` then `diffuseTexture = solid` shades through the render target or aborts, and the reverse order leaks the solid texel's bytes plus a spurious uv_invert_y into a render-target draw. Pre-existing, and this branch was adding the fourth writer to it. Fixed at the TYPE level rather than per arm: one take_standard_diffuse_slot empties both representations and returns the slot, and all four arms take it through that -- the render-target arm setting its mark after. The same two-representation lesson as the earlier TransformNode case, where per-sink patches were whack-a-mole

the SolidTexture-to-1x1 TextureData normalization was hand-written three times -- node_material_texture(SolidTexture), set_pbr_occlusion_solid_texture and the new set_standard_diffuse_solid_texture -- and had ALREADY diverged: the occlusion copy set no sampler at all while the other two set six lines of it. The branch's answer had been a generation-time assertion that the pin still calls getBilinearSampler, which checks N restatements rather than removing N-1 of them and cannot see a divergence that already exists. Now one generator constant, emitted static into each consuming unit

MEASURED CORRECTION to the finding above, from the sweep. The first fix shared the DEFINITION across translation units, on the verified claim that createSolidTexture2D reaches texture:file unconditionally and texture_file.cpp is gated on exactly that. True, and not sufficient: a node material reaches a solid texture through the block loader rather than through that intrinsic, so texture_file.cpp is absent from scenes 60/61/64/77/78/79 and lld-link reported an undefined bbl::solid_texture_data for all six. The sharing is at GENERATION instead -- one string with internal linkage per emitting unit -- which removes the divergence without a cross-gate link dependency. Verified by building the node case, the solid-arm case, two PBR scenes and the plugin scene

take_standard_diffuse_slot was emitted under only the render-target arm's gate while the pixels, solid and file arms call it -- scene 272 reaches the solid arm with no render-target arm and failed to compile with an undeclared identifier. Caught by the sweep, not by any targeted build: the gate matrix is what needs exercising after a gating change, which is why the rule is to build a scene reaching NONE of a gated feature

the entry statement list was the one of six statement-list emitters missing the terminator break, and this branch widened its trigger: before it only inline query reads folded, and now any helper the reference query answers does -- which is exactly where the corpus family writes `if (captureFrame === null) { return; }` at main() level. Without the break, statements generation has proved unreachable are still lowered, and features they reach (a deterministic-random among them) still recorded

the Math fold arm named `round` directly while option-helpers.ts already exports foldableMathUnary, the table staticNumberValue folds through, whose header states the POLICY for which Math functions may fold. That left the file internally inconsistent: the taint rule twenty lines up treats every Math.* call over a resolved browser value alike, so Math.floor over the pinned query was neither tainted nor foldable. It now reads the table, and the two rules cannot disagree. The same finding's other half -- that the arm inlined a FOURTH copy of a default-library method-call shape test -- did not survive checking: two of the three cited copies are bare-identifier tests (Number(...), isNaN(...)), a different shape, and only the Math taint rule shares it

the released-world liveness test was stated twice -- once throwing in world_at, once open-coded in body_speed_limit to answer without throwing. Now one world_or_null holding the triple, with world_at as that plus a throw

the speed-limit clamp was written out verbatim at three call sites, each widening two btScalars to double through the PAL's wire struct only for the callee to narrow them back. One clamp_body_velocity(BodyEntry&) overload beside the existing one collapses all three; the architecture test that pinned the old spelling now pins the limit's SOURCE instead
physics_world_release restated physics_world_remove_body's whole tail, added four lines above it in the same commit. It now calls it, so the two cannot drift about what detaching a body means
place_body restated fo_sync_node_to_body's entire body fourteen lines below it. It now calls it, matching the same commit's own write_node_pose factoring

gc_regions materialised a heap-allocated vector of every body's region handle only to std::find in it, once per step for the whole life of a world past its first migration. Asking each candidate region directly with std::any_of stops at the first body that keeps it and allocates nothing

PhysicsRegion::gravity was written at both construction sites and read nowhere -- getRegionGravity is its only pinned reader and was correctly dropped as unreachable, so the field should have gone with it

assertMeshAccumulatorShapes re-implemented assertShapeContracts, which the same commit generalized 130 lines above it. Its stated reason (a class METHOD is out of pinnedDeclaration's reach) did not hold: the walk needs only a root to search and an owner to blame, both ts.Node. It is now a table row with the module file as its resolver

the runtime error for a body naming no floating-origin region named region RECLAIM as the cause, which is the one thing that did not happen when the real cause is a body created before enableHavokFloatingOrigin. The message now names both causes. The deeper fix -- a generation-time refusal, with context.boundPixelsTextures as the in-repo precedent for a spent-local mark -- is recorded rather than built

floating origin multiplies the PAL's global body scans by region count: physics_world_step walks the whole bodies() deque filtering on entry.world, eight times per 1/60s step once Havok's 1/240s substep is counted, so 8N becomes 8RN and each region re-scans every other region's bodies only to skip them. A body_indices vector on WorldEntry would fix it -- all three membership transitions are already centralised. Recorded in TODO.md with the measurement rather than applied: invasive, touching pre-existing code, and unreached by any registered scene
findings.blockedBy: The 8RN cost is derived from the call path, not measured: no registered scene reaches a multi-region floating-origin world with enough bodies for the scan to show up, so there is no before/after number to hold the change to. Somebody must build that scene and time it first.

findings.summary: region_at is a linear scan run per body per step purely to recover an origin the body's own record could carry beside region, which has exactly two writers and both already hold it. Recorded, not applied: it adds a field that must stay in sync, which is the derivable-state defect the same review flags elsewhere
findings.blockedBy: Same missing measurement as the body-index list it belongs with, and the fix adds a second copy of the origin that must stay in sync with body.region -- derivable state, which is the defect class this same review flagged elsewhere. Wrong trade without a number showing the scan matters.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, the physics-lane entry, beside the body-index note

findings.summary: physics_shape_create_mesh feeds btTriangleMesh triangle-by-triangle, de-indexing the indexed soup append_physics_mesh_geometry just built -- roughly 6x the vertex memory on a closed mesh, and a correspondingly larger array for buildBvh. btTriangleIndexVertexArray over the two vectors already in hand would keep the indexing. Recorded, not applied: it changes the array the BVH is built over, and scene 102 is measured at 0.003 immediately before a sweep
findings.blockedBy: It changes the vertex array Bullet builds the BVH over, and nobody has measured whether contact results move with it. Scene 102 is the only mesh-collider gate, it sits at 0.003, and this was raised immediately before the validation sweep.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, the physics-lane entry, beside the body-index note

findings.summary: keying helperBinding by ts.Symbol instead of by identifier text plus a pos/end containment test would remove the second, weaker scope mechanism standing beside the compiler's own -- BrowserErasureContext would need a valueSymbol accessor it does not expose. Correctly noted that the comment cites static-evaluator.ts as precedent where that passage argues the opposite. Recorded, not applied: it widens a context interface for no measured defect
findings.blockedBy: BrowserErasureContext exposes no symbol resolver, so this widens a shared context interface -- and no scene has been shown to shadow a helper binding with a module constant of the same name, which is the defect it would prevent. The containment guard is measured to be load-bearing today.
